transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
New York's Democratic governor has appointed a special prosecutor in the case of a woman
who says she was gang-raped at Cornell University Fraternity in 2024.
Steve Kastenbaum reports the investigation was initially closed without any charges brought.
Governor Kathy Hochul says the young woman was failed by the people obligated to protect
her.
I will not allow anyone to sweep this case under the rug.
We are ensuring that all the facts of this case are brought into the light.
It will now be up to State Attorney General Letitia James to determine whether any of
the seven accused fraternity members will face criminal charges.
We will review the facts, gather evidence, interview witnesses, and if warranted, pursue
prosecutions.
The governor says she lost faith in the local prosecutor's ability to handle the case.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Kastenbaum in New York.
Krista Pike's attorney says she's still in a hospital unconscious and on a ventilator
after a failed execution in Tennessee on Wednesday.
Pike was sentenced to death for a murder she committed at age 18.
She would have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years.
Republican Governor Bill Lee has ordered an independent review and paused executions.
President Trump will host a rally this evening in Mobile, Alabama, his second stop of a multi-state
campaign blitz ahead of next month's midterm elections and Piers Franco Ordonez reports
he's starting in friendlier red states before visiting more competitive races.
Trump says the midterm elections will come down to 35 competitive races, and he's vowed
to campaign in every one.
But his first three stops are in deeply red states, Texas, Oklahoma, and now Alabama.
The president says he's visiting Alabama to thank voters for their ongoing support, but
even pollster John McHenry sees a more practical benefit.
Some of it is just knocking the rust off and having your campaign speech in a friendly
environment before you go into some other places that are a little bit more of a swing
state.
Trump will go to Ohio next.
Franco, Ordonez, NPR News, the White House.
The average price of jet fuel climbed in September to the highest level on record, NPR's Joel
Rose reports.
The average price for a gallon of jet fuel climbed to $4.37 in September, according to
the tracking firm Argus.
Airlines for America, the industry trade group that represents the major airlines, says that
sets a new all-time high, narrowly eclipsing the previous record set in April, shortly
after the war in Iran began.
The group says airlines are cutting flights and retiring older aircraft to keep costs down,
but carriers are also passing some of their fuel costs on to the consumer.
The average domestic airfare has reached its highest point of the year, according to the
travel website Kayak, at more than $400, with the holiday travel season looming.
Joel Rose, NPR News, Washington.
U.S. stocks rose today.
The S&P 500 climbed nearly three-quarters of a percent.
This is NPR News.
Brazil's President Luis Anacio Lula da Silva and opposition candidate Flavio Bolsonaro
have turned down a final chance to debate ahead of the election, the move to prize 158
million voters ahead of the first round of voting on Sunday.
It's the first time in 20 years that Brazil's leading candidates have rejected any public
confrontation.
Bolsonaro is the son of former president and Trump ally Jair Bolsonaro, who's in jail for
attempting a coup after he lost the 2022 election.
Russian President Vladimir Putin is warning the West against further escalating tensions
over Ukraine.
His remarks came at a foreign policy forum outside Moscow, as NPR's Charles Maines reports.
In his address, Putin cast Russia as a victim of Western aggression over the years, saying
NATO had taken advantage of Russian goodwill following the breakup of the Soviet Union,
and later Putin claimed forced Russian to its current war in Ukraine.
The Kremlin leader signaled that conflict would continue.
Putin effectively rejected recent U.S. proposals for Russia and Ukraine to halt strikes on
energy and shipping this winter.
He also said any future peace depended on Ukraine first surrendering additional land
Russian forces have failed to seize in more than four-and-a-half years of war.
That demand came as he warned the West.
Moscow was ready to use its nuclear arsenal if Russia felt its own territory was ever
under threat.
Charles Maines, NPR News, Moscow.
A man found a six-carat diamond in Arkansas' crater of diamonds state park.
Jack Peridin calls it "American Dream," an independent appraiser says it could sell for
about $250,000.
The park is one of the only places in the world where the public can dig for and keep
their diamonds.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: New York Governor Hochul appoints special prosecutor for Cornell University fraternity gang rape case from 2024
Krista Pike remains unconscious on ventilator after failed execution in Tennessee on Wednesday
President Trump hosts campaign rally in Mobile, Alabama, second stop of multi-state midterm campaign blitz
Average price of jet fuel climbs to record $4.37 per gallon in September
Brazil's President Lula and opposition candidate Bolsonaro decline to debate ahead of Sunday election
Russian President Putin warns West against escalating Ukraine tensions at Moscow foreign policy forum
Man finds six-carat diamond worth approximately $250,000 at Arkansas' Crater of Diamonds State Park
